question: Will AfD win the most seats in the Baden-Württemberg Landtag election?
summary: Ensemble baseline is 2%; polls show CDU lead with AfD around 19–21% and Greens near 20–23%, making AfD unlikely to be the largest party in BW.
Historical precedent: AfD has never led BW; Greens or CDU have led in recent elections, anchoring the base probability near 0–5%.
Per-persona signals are heavily skewed toward low probability; the 8% contrarian view is treated as noise rather than a durable signal.
No credible threshold breach is evident; objections support a low-probability forecast and do not justify raising the ensemble.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid in confirming the low-probability outcome but do not reveal a systematic bias or a plausible path to AfD leading in seats.
justification.adjustment: No adjustment; maintain the ensemble baseline as the calibrated probability.

forecasts.reference-class: Baden-Württemberg Landtag elections where the CDU or Greens have historically won the most seats; AfD has not led a BW Landtag in recent elections (e.g., 2021 result: Greens largest party, AfD well below 20%).

sources.claim: Infratest dimap poll reported by SWP shows CDU around 29%, Greens around 23%, and AfD around 20% five months before the 2026 election.
BWTrend poll indicates CDU ~29%, AfD ~21%, Greens ~20% (AfD ahead of Greens for the first time in this survey).
Polymarket prediction market places second place around Greens ~21-23% with CDU ~29-32% and AfD ~20% (as of Feb 2026).
2021 Baden-Württemberg Landtag results: Greens 32.6%, CDU 24.1%, AfD 9.7%.
INSA poll (Feb 2026) shows CDU 28%, Grünen 22%, AfD 20%, SPD 10%, Die Linke 7%, FDP 6%, BSW 3%.
INSA poll (January 27, 2026): CDU 29%, Grüne 21%, AfD 20%, SPD 10%, Die Linke 7%, FDP 5%.
INSA poll (February 23, 2026): CDU 28%, Grüne 22%, AfD 20%, SPD 10%, Die Linke 7%, FDP 6%, BSW 3%.
Election date is 8 March 2026; 120 seats in the Landtag; polls indicate CDU/Greens lead with AfD around 20% rather than leading.
Aktuelle Umfragen im Überblick: CDU ~29%, Gröne ~23%, AfD ~20% (Stand Januar 2026).
BWTrend (Infratest dimap für ARD) Ende Februar 2026: CDU  ~29%, AfD ~21%, Grüne ~20%; AfD auf einem der vorderen Ränge, aber nicht offensichtlich die größte Partei.
WELT-Bericht (Feb 2026) zusammenfassend: CDU 27%, Gröne 25%, AfD 19% in ARD/Infratest dimap.

causal-factors.name: CDU polling lead over AfD
causal-factors.rationale: Polls consistently place CDU around 27–29% while AfD sits near 19–21%, making AfD unlikely to be the largest party.

causal-factors.name: Greens' vote share near AfD in several polls
causal-factors.rationale: Greens polling in the low to mid-20s keeps AfD from surpassing both major rivals to lead the Landtag.

causal-factors.name: Occasional AfD lead over Greens in BWTrend
causal-factors.rationale: BWTrend has shown AfD ahead of Greens in some instances, signaling a non-negligible upside risk even if not sustained.

causal-factors.name: Strong historical baseline: AfD has never led BW Landtag
causal-factors.rationale: Historical results (e.g., 2021 Greens largest; AfD far behind) impose a base-rate that disfavors AfD leading in seats.

causal-factors.name: Multi-party competition dampens single-party dominance
causal-factors.rationale: With CDU and Greens competing closely and AfD not consistently ahead, securing the most seats remains unlikely.

causal-factors.name: CDU remains the leading party in polls
causal-factors.rationale: Polls place CDU around 28–29% with Greens near 21–23% and AfD around 20%; for AfD to be the largest party, it would have to surpass both CDU and Greens, which current trends make unlikely unless CDU weakens substantially.

causal-factors.name: Greens' support near parity but potentially volatile
causal-factors.rationale: Greens sometimes trail AfD in close polls or close the gap; a stronger Greens performance or confirmation of Greens' lead relative to AfD would push AfD further from being largest.

causal-factors.name: AfD turnout surge or late swing
causal-factors.rationale: A late uptick in AfD support or higher turnout among its voters could lift AfD above Greens or even threaten CDU's lead in votes and seats.

causal-factors.name: Greens leadership transition (Kretschmann retirement) destabilizing Greens
causal-factors.rationale: Incumbent Greens' advantage could erode after Kretschmann's retirement, potentially shrinking Greens' lead and benefiting AfD in a tight race.

causal-factors.name: Polls understate AfD support or turnout effects
causal-factors.rationale: If actual support or turnout for AfD exceeds poll estimates, AfD could close the gap with or even surpass the other leading parties.

causal-factors.name: CDU polling lead in Baden-Württemberg
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple late-January to February 2026 polls place CDU around the high 20s (roughly 27–29%), well ahead of AfD (~19–21%), reducing AfD’s likelihood of being the largest party.

causal-factors.name: AfD gains relative to Greens in some polls
causal-factors.rationale: In at least one BW-specific poll (e.g., BWTrend/Infratest dimap–ARD variants) AfD has briefly surpassed Greens, narrowing the gap and increasing upside risk if that dynamic persists.

causal-factors.name: Historical precedent in Baden-Württemberg
causal-factors.rationale: The reference-class history shows AfD has never been the largest party in BW, with Greens or CDU typically leading, anchoring the base probability at a very low level.

causal-factors.name: Poll uncertainty and late-stage dynamics
causal-factors.rationale: Polls vary by methodology and date; while late shifts could occur, current data do not indicate a credible path for AfD to overtake CDU as the largest party.

synthesis: Polls and history jointly indicate AfD leading BW in seats is very unlikely; the ensemble of 2% remains a credible final probability given no threshold breach and little upside in objections.
